answer: An agent market hires cleaning robots for an ivory-tiled terrace above a lagoon. Each shift requires a remotely attested controller with one active lease token; the scheduler consumes that token and rejects bids from other accounts using the same machine. Opening aliases yields no extra shifts. An attacker must rent additional robots, pay for power and upkeep, and post a damage bond for each. A stolen vendor signing key could forge controllers, while a wealthy fleet can still dominate, so independent spot inspections and per-operator caps remain necessary.
